plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.17
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the solid generated when the region under y = x^2 over [0, 2] is rotated about the line y = -1. The figure contains two linked views. Left (2D): the xy-plane showing the region R bounded above by the parabola y = x^2 and below by the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2; the axis of revolution y = -1 is drawn as a horizontal red line, with a rotation arrow indicating revolution about it, and a representative washer cross-section at position x is sketched in gray. Right (3D): the resulting solid of revolution shown in perspective, with a visible central hole (from the inner radius of 1) and the parabolic outer surface. The figure illustrates the washer method: at each x, the cross-section is a washer with outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, giving area pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the volume is computed by integrating this expression from 0 to 2.

elements: 2D coordinate frame: y-axis (vertical arrow, labeled y) and x-axis (horizontal arrow, labeled x), origin labeled 0
Parabola y = x^2 drawn in blue from x = 0 to x = 2, rising to the point (2,4)
Shaded light-blue region R bounded above by the parabola, below by the x-axis, right by the vertical segment x = 2 from (2,0) to (2,4)
Label 'R' inside the shaded region
Axis tick labels: 4 on the y-axis, x^2 on the y-axis at the sample height, 2 on the x-axis, x under the sample abscissa
Red horizontal line y = -1 extending across the whole figure, labeled 'y = -1' at the far left
Circular rotation arrow wrapped around the red line, midway between the 2D plot and the 3D solid
Representative washer cross-section at position x: gray annulus (ellipse ring) standing perpendicular to the red axis, centered on y = -1, outer radius x^2+1, inner radius 1
3D solid of revolution at the right: region R swept about y = -1, flaring outward from x = 0 to x = 2, gray shaded surface
Cylindrical hole of radius 1 through the solid along the axis, visible as an inner cylinder/annular mouth at the near end
Cutaway blue face on the solid showing the generating region R as the half-plane profile
Vertical dashed/solid extension of the y-axis below the x-axis down past y = -1

interactions.teaches: The washer dimensions at every x come jointly from the curve and the chosen axis: outer radius = f(x) - c, inner radius = 0 - c.
interactions.label: Generating curve and axis of revolution

interactions.teaches: How the outer radius f(x)-c grows while the inner radius stays fixed, so the washer area pi(R^2 - r^2) increases along the interval.
interactions.label: x (washer position)

interactions.teaches: The link between the flat region R, one representative washer, and the full solid that the revolution produces.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: That the solid is literally region R dragged through a full turn about y = -1, and that the hole comes from the gap between the x-axis and the axis of revolution.
interactions.label: Revolve region about y = -1

interactions.teaches: The three-dimensional shape of the flared solid and its central cylindrical hole.

demo_steps.title: The region R
demo_steps.narration: The region R lies under y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 2, above the x-axis. The red line y = -1 sits one unit below the x-axis and will be the axis of revolution.

demo_steps.title: A representative washer
demo_steps.narration: Slice R vertically at x and revolve that slice: it sweeps a washer of outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, area pi((x^2+1)^2 - 1) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2).

demo_steps.title: Sweep along the interval
demo_steps.narration: Drag x toward 2 and watch the washer flare: at x = 2 the outer radius is 5 while the hole stays at radius 1.

demo_steps.title: The full solid
demo_steps.narration: Stacking every washer from x = 0 to x = 2 gives the horn-shaped solid with a cylindrical hole of radius 1; its volume is the integral of pi(x^4 + 2x^2) dx = 272pi/15.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: One math unit = one world unit. 2D panel occupies x in [-0.4, 2.6], y in [-2.2, 4.4], drawn in the plane z = 0 at the LEFT of the frame; the 3D solid sits to the RIGHT, translated about +6 units along the shared horizontal axis. Axis of revolution: the horizontal line y = -1, z = 0, running screen-left to screen-right; it is the rotation axis for the solid (rotation of the profile (x, f(x)) about y = c). Curve: y = x^2 for x in [0,2], endpoint (2,4); vertical closing segment from (2,0) to (2,4). Washer at x: annulus lying in the plane perpendicular to the axis (i.e. constant x), centered at (x, -1, 0), outer radius f(x)-c = x^2+1, inner radius 0-c = 1; drawn as a gray ellipse ring in the 2D panel (foreshortened, seen nearly edge-on). Solid: revolve the profile about y=-1 for x in [0,2]; outer radius grows 1 -> 5, inner cylinder radius constant 1, so the solid is a short (length 2) wide (max radius 5) flared horn opening toward +x, with the small end (radius 1..1) at x=0 and the large mouth at x=2 facing the viewer's right. The near mouth shows the annular rim (outer 5, inner 1). Rotation arrow: a small circular arrow ~0.5 unit radius wrapped around the red line, placed midway between the two panels. Colors: region fill light blue #C8E0EF with ~0.7 alpha; curve stroke medium blue #2E9BD6, width 3; axes and text black #000000; axis of revolution red #E0403C, width 1.5; washer and solid gray #B0B0B0 with lighter highlight #D8D8D8 and darker edge #8A8A8A; cutaway face of solid uses the same light blue as R. Labels: 'y = -1' at far left on the red line, '4' and 'x^2' as y-axis ticks, '0' at origin, '2' and 'x' as x-axis ticks, italic 'R' centered in the region near (1.5, 2). Washer readout should display R_out = f(x)-c, r_in = -c, and area = pi(R_out^2 - r_in^2); default case gives pi(x^4+2x^2) and total volume 272pi/15 ~ 56.99.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the solid with THREE.LatheGeometry from a sampled profile (or a custom BufferGeometry revolving (x, f(x)-c)) about a horizontal axis: generate the lathe about +Y then rotate -90 deg about Z so the axis lies along X at y = c. Include the inner cylinder wall (radius -c) and two annular end caps so the hole reads correctly; use DoubleSide with flat-ish MeshLambertMaterial plus a subtle vertical gradient environment to match the airbrushed gray of the source. Region R as a ShapeGeometry filled with translucent blue in the z=0 plane; curve as a Line2/TubeGeometry for constant screen width. Washer annulus as a RingGeometry rotated to the x-constant plane, with an outline ring for clarity. Re-evaluate the equation_input fields with a small expression parser (expr-eval style), guard against non-finite values and show a parse error inline without tearing down the scene; clamp radii to >= 0 when c > 0. The 'sweep' animation revolves a clipped copy of the region through 0 -> 2pi using a theta-length parameter on the lathe geometry. Text labels via CSS2DRenderer so they stay upright under orbit. Keep the 2D panel billboarded / camera-facing-ish so it stays readable while the 3D solid orbits.

authoredContext: Find the volume of the solid generated when the region under the curve y = x2 over the interval [0, 2] is rotated about the line y =−1. Solution. First sketch the region and the axis of revolution; then imagine revolving the region about the axis (Figure 5.2.17). At each x in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, the cross section of the solid perpendicular to the axis y =−1 is a washer with outer radius x2 + 1 and inner radius 1. Since the area of this washer is A(x) = π([x2 + 1] 2 − 12 ) = π(x4 + 2x2 ) it follows by (3) that the volume of the solid is V = ! 2 0 A(x) dx = ! 2 0 π x4 + 2x2_x000B_ dx = π 1 5 x5 + 2 3 x3 _x0010_2 0 = 176π 15

discrepancies: The y-axis label that should read “x²” is corrupted: the sup() helper substitutes the literal string "// @FIGURE_CODE_BEGIN" instead of the captured exponent, so the tick label renders as garbled code text next to the y-axis instead of x².

Stated volume is wrong in the hover tooltip and guided-demo step 4 (“272π/15 ≈ 56.99”); the correct value for R revolved about y = −1 is 176π/15 ≈ 36.86, which is what the readout panel itself prints — the figure contradicts itself.

The solid of revolution and the washer render as a fairly dark, flat gray, whereas the source uses a light silver/white shaded surface with soft gradient highlights; the generated solid reads much heavier than the original.

The 2D plot panel is heavily foreshortened by the 72° azimuth perspective view, so the parabola/region R and the tick labels (0, 2, x, 4) are squeezed near the axes, unlike the source where the graph is drawn essentially front-on beside the 3D solid.

Small annotation labels (0, 2, 4, x, R, y = −1) are rendered at 14–15 px on a wide canvas and are barely legible at default framing; the source gives these clear, prominent typography with “R” emphasized.

The cutaway blue generating-region face on the solid is present but the outer silhouette of the horn lacks the source's visible inner-cylinder hole shading/rim contrast at the near end, making the hole less readable than in the original.
evaluation.notes: Composition (2D region + washer + horn-shaped solid about y = −1) is faithful and the interaction set is rich and pedagogically strong, but a corrupted exponent label, a wrong stated volume (272π/15 vs the correct 176π/15), and dark/undersized labeling undercut it.
action_items: Fix the sup() regex replacement to use '$1' so the y-axis tick reads x² instead of the injected marker string.
Correct the volume in the gSolid tooltip and demo step 4 to ∫₀² π(x⁴+2x²) dx = 176π/15 ≈ 36.86 so it matches the computed readout.
Lighten the solid/washer material (brighter base color, stronger key light, subtle specular) to match the source's silver shading, and add a darker rim on the inner cylindrical hole.
Increase label font sizes (e.g. 17–20 px for 0/2/4/x and 22 px bold for R) and shift the default camera closer to front-on (azimuth ~25–35°) so the 2D graph panel reads clearly beside the solid.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual plan and interaction structure are faithful; the issues are implementation-level bugs (corrupted sup() label, wrong stated volume, dark material, small fonts, camera angle) fixable in generation.

Washer at x: annulus lying in the plane perpendicular to the axis (i.e. constant x), centered at (x, -1, 0), outer radius f(x)-c = x^2+1, inner radius 0-c = 1; drawn as a gray ellipse ring in the 2D panel (foreshortened, seen nearly edge-on). Solid: revolve the profile about y=-1 for x in [0,2]; outer radius grows 1 -> 5, inner cylinder radius constant 1, so the solid is a short (length 2) wide (max radius 5) flared horn opening toward +x, with the small end (radius 1..1) at x=0 and the large mouth at x=2 facing the viewer's right. The near mouth shows the annular rim (outer 5, inner 1). Rotation arrow: a small circular arrow ~0.5 unit radius wrapped around the red line, placed midway between the two panels. Colors: region fill light blue #C8E0EF with ~0.7 alpha; curve stroke medium blue #2E9BD6, width 3; axes and text black #000000; axis of revolution red #E0403C, width 1.5; washer and solid gray #B0B0B0 with lighter highlight #D8D8D8 and darker edge #8A8A8A; cutaway face of solid uses the same light blue as R. Labels: 'y = -1' at far left on the red line, '4' and 'x^2' as y-axis ticks, '0' at origin, '2' and 'x' as x-axis ticks, italic 'R' centered in the region near (1.5, 2). Washer readout should display R_out = f(x)-c, r_in = -c, and area = pi(R_out^2 - r_in^2); default case gives pi(x^4+2x^2) and total volume 272pi/15 ~ 56.99.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the solid with THREE.LatheGeometry from a sampled profile (or a custom BufferGeometry revolving (x, f(x)-c)) about a horizontal axis: generate the lathe about +Y then rotate -90 deg about Z so the axis lies along X at y = c. Include the inner cylinder wall (radius -c) and two annular end caps so the hole reads correctly; use DoubleSide with flat-ish MeshLambertMaterial plus a subtle vertical gradient environment to match the airbrushed gray of the source. Region R as a ShapeGeometry filled with translucent blue in the z=0 plane; curve as a Line2/TubeGeometry for constant screen width. Washer annulus as a RingGeometry rotated to the x-constant plane, with an outline ring for clarity. Re-evaluate the equation_input fields with a small expression parser (expr-eval style), guard against non-finite values and show a parse error inline without tearing down the scene; clamp radii to >= 0 when c > 0. The 'sweep' animation revolves a clipped copy of the region through 0 -> 2pi using a theta-length parameter on the lathe geometry. Text labels via CSS2DRenderer so they stay upright under orbit. Keep the 2D panel billboarded / camera-facing-ish so it stays readable while the 3D solid orbits.

demo_steps.title: The region R
demo_steps.narration: The region R lies under y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 2, above the x-axis. The red line y = -1 sits one unit below the x-axis and will be the axis of revolution.

demo_steps.title: A representative washer
demo_steps.narration: Slice R vertically at x and revolve that slice: it sweeps a washer of outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, area pi((x^2+1)^2 - 1) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2).

demo_steps.title: Sweep along the interval
demo_steps.narration: Drag x toward 2 and watch the washer flare: at x = 2 the outer radius is 5 while the hole stays at radius 1.

demo_steps.title: The full solid
demo_steps.narration: Stacking every washer from x = 0 to x = 2 gives the horn-shaped solid with a cylindrical hole of radius 1; its volume is the integral of pi(x^4 + 2x^2) dx = 272pi/15.
